```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Case-study numbers and figures come from the recorded multi-arm result
# files; the walkthrough slides execute the sixteen-verb workflow live on
# a simulated cohort.
library(ggplot2)
library(cleanTMLE)
.ma <- "../rescueCo/results/multiarm"
.rd <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path(.ma, f)
  if (file.exists(p)) read.csv(p, check.names = FALSE) else NULL
}
cs_sup <- .rd("support_by_contrast.csv")
cs_ncl <- .rd("nc_ladder.csv")
cs_lad <- .rd("ladder_estimates.csv")
if (is.null(cs_lad)) {
  ck <- list.files(.ma, pattern = "^ladder_.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(ck)) cs_lad <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ck, readRDS))
}
.rds <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path(.ma, f)
  if (file.exists(p)) readRDS(p) else NULL
}
cs_cmp <- rbind(
  if (!is.null(x <- .rds("designcmp_C1.rds"))) cbind(contrast = "C1 (severe overlap)", x),
  if (!is.null(x <- .rds("designcmp_PRIMARY.rds"))) cbind(contrast = "Primary cohort (good overlap)", x))
cs_lock1 <- {
  p <- file.path(.ma, "multiarm_locks.rds")
  if (file.exists(p)) readRDS(p)[["C1"]] else NULL
}
cs_lite1 <- .rds("design_lite_C1.rds")
okabe <- c(PASS = "#009E73", FLAG = "#E69F00", SEVERE = "#D55E00",
           FAIL = "#B22222")
thm <- theme_minimal(base_size = 17) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_blank())
```

## Two problems with observational comparisons

- Problem 1: the analyst can see how each modelling choice changes the estimate, and picks accordingly.
- Problem 2: some comparisons cannot be estimated from the data at all, but the software still returns a number and a confidence interval.

A clean-room design deals with problem 1. cleanTMLE also deals with problem 2, and does it before anyone sees the outcome.

## This talk

1. Why this matters, with one of our own analyses as the cautionary example
2. How the package works: a walkthrough on simulated data
3. What the simulation study showed
4. The Rescue.Co ambulance study in Nairobi
5. How this compares with existing tools

# 1. Why this matters

## Problem 1: choices made after seeing the outcome

- No analysis plan covers every decision. Cells turn out sparse, a model fails to converge, a variable is missing more often than expected.
- If the analyst makes those decisions after looking at the treatment-outcome association, the analysis is no longer prespecified, whatever the plan said.
- Muntner et al. (2024) propose a fix: one team builds the cohort and runs the diagnostics without access to the outcome, and a second team does the estimation.

## Problem 2: the comparison cannot be estimated

- The average treatment effect compares everyone treated with everyone untreated. That only makes sense if every kind of patient could plausibly have ended up in either group.
- If a whole group of patients almost never gets one of the treatments, the estimator does not stop. It extrapolates into that group and reports a number.
- Truncating the weights makes the interval narrower. It does not add any information about those patients.
- Blinding does not help with this. A blinded team can still commit to a question the data cannot answer.

## This happened to us

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Adjusted estimate, effect on time to ambulance arrival**

**+14,637 minutes**

with a narrow confidence interval
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Crude difference**

**about 7 hours faster**

Same cohort. A large group of patients almost never used the service we were studying. Nothing in the model output pointed to a problem.
:::
::::

## What the blind phase should establish

1. The cohort, treatment, outcome, and follow-up window were fixed in advance.
2. The planned comparison can be estimated. If not, which nearby estimand can be.
3. The estimator was chosen in advance and tested against realistic data problems.
4. If the estimand changed, it changed by a rule written down beforehand, and the change is logged.

`design_report()` collects the evidence for all four into one document for the review team.

# 2. How the package works

## The package: sixteen functions, one lock object

Each function takes the lock as its input. Only the functions in the last box read the outcome. The next slides run through this on a simulated dataset.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
flowchart LR
    A["Lock<br/>create_analysis_lock<br/>declare_negative_controls<br/>declare_estimand_ladder"] --> B["Estimability<br/>fit_ps<br/>assess_support<br/>estimand_feasibility<br/>simulate_support"]
    B --> C["Candidates<br/>define_candidates<br/>stress_test<br/>select_candidate"]
    C --> D["Residual confounding<br/>negative_control_ladder<br/>check_process_indicators"]
    D --> E["Review<br/>design_report<br/>export_design_log"]
    E --> F["Estimate<br/>estimate_effect<br/>run_estimand_ladder"]
    style A fill:#e6f0fa,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style B fill:#e6f0fa,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style C fill:#e6f0fa,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style D fill:#e6f0fa,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style E fill:#e6f0fa,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style F fill:#fde8d8,stroke:#333,color:#000
```

## Step 1: create the lock

The lock holds the data, the variable roles, the decision thresholds, and a hash of all of it. The outcome column is kept in a separate store that only the estimation functions can read.

```{r wt-lock, echo = TRUE}
dat  <- sim_func1(n = 1000, seed = 42)
lock <- create_analysis_lock(
  dat, "treatment", "event_24",
  covariates        = c("age", "sex", "biomarker", "comorbidity"),
  negative_controls = "nc_outcome",
  dq_thresholds = list(max_abs_bias = 0.02,
                       min_coverage = 0.90, max_rmse_ratio = 1.5),
  nc_criteria   = list(null_band = 0.02),
  seed = 42, enforce = TRUE)
lock <- declare_estimand_ladder(lock, primary = "ATE",
          fallbacks = c("trimmed_ATE", "ATT"), trigger = "SEVERE")
```

## Step 2: check overlap

`assess_support()` grades the overlap in the fitted propensity score as PASS, FLAG, SEVERE, or FAIL.

```{r wt-support, echo = TRUE, results = "hide"}
ps  <- fit_ps(lock, method = "glm")
sup <- assess_support(ps)
fea <- estimand_feasibility(ps)
```

```{r wt-support-fig, fig.height = 4}
plot(sup) + thm + theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15))
```

## Step 2, continued: which estimands are feasible

```{r wt-feas-table}
knitr::kable(fea$table[, c("estimand", "max_weight",
                           "ess_treated", "verdict")],
             digits = 1)
```

## Step 3: stress-test the candidate estimators

Each candidate is fitted to simulated datasets with the declared data problems applied. The plot shows absolute bias against severity.

```{r wt-stress, echo = TRUE, results = "hide"}
cands <- define_candidates(grid = list(
  truncations = 0.01,
  libraries   = list(glm = "SL.glm", glm_mean = c("SL.glm", "SL.mean"))))
st <- stress_test(lock, cands, reps = 20, verbose = FALSE,
  threats = list(
    covariate_missingness_mnar = list(fractions = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)),
    unmeasured_confounding = list(
      U_prevalence = 0.2, U_treatment_OR = c(1.5, 2, 3),
      U_outcome_OR = c(1.5, 2, 3))))
```

```{r wt-stress-fig, fig.height = 3.6}
plot(st, metric = "bias") + thm +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("^OR_trt([0-9.]+)_out.*$", "OR \\1", x)) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 15))
```

## Step 3, continued: pick a candidate by the prespecified rule

```{r wt-select, echo = TRUE, results = "hide"}
best <- select_candidate(st, rule = "min_max_rmse")
lock <- declare_estimand_ladder(lock, primary = "ATE",
          fallbacks = c("trimmed_ATE", "ATT"),
          trigger = "SEVERE", candidate = best)
```

Selected: `r best$candidate_id`. The verdicts come from simulated outcomes and thresholds that were fixed in the lock, so the real treatment effect had no influence on the choice.

```{r wt-verdict-table}
knitr::kable(st$verdict[, c("candidate", "worst_abs_bias",
                            "worst_coverage", "verdict")], digits = 3)
```

## Step 4: sign off and unmask

With `enforce = TRUE`, the estimation functions refuse to run until someone unmasks the outcome and gives their name. The name goes into the design log.

```{r wt-log, echo = TRUE}
masked <- mask_outcome(lock)
lock   <- unmask_outcome(masked, lock,
                         approved_by = "review team")
```

```{r wt-log-table}
lg <- export_design_log(lock, format = "muntner")
knitr::kable(tail(lg[, c("stage", "decision", "decided_by")], 3))
```

## Step 5: estimate

`run_estimand_ladder()` estimates the primary if it is feasible and every feasible fallback. Each row carries its overlap verdict.

```{r wt-estimate, echo = TRUE, results = "hide"}
fit <- run_estimand_ladder(lock, ps)
```

```{r wt-estimate-fig, fig.height = 3.4}
plot(fit) + thm + labs(subtitle = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## Same propensity score, four estimands, different weights

```{r fig-weights, fig.cap = "Implied weights on the protocol contrast, one point per patient, log scale. The ATE needs weights up to 257; the effect among the treated (ATT) is bounded at 5 by the largest propensity; the overlap-weighted ATO never exceeds 1."}
if (!is.null(cs_lock1) && !is.null(cs_lite1)) {
  g <- pmin(pmax(cs_lite1$ps_raw, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  A <- as.integer(cs_lock1$data[[cs_lock1$treatment]])
  wd <- rbind(
    data.frame(estimand = "ATE", w = ifelse(A == 1, 1 / g, 1 / (1 - g))),
    data.frame(estimand = "Trimmed ATE",
               w = { keep <- g >= 0.05 & g <= 0.95
                     ifelse(A[keep] == 1, 1 / g[keep], 1 / (1 - g[keep])) }),
    data.frame(estimand = "ATT", w = ifelse(A == 1, 1, g / (1 - g))),
    data.frame(estimand = "ATO", w = ifelse(A == 1, 1 - g, g)))
  wd$estimand <- factor(wd$estimand,
                        levels = c("ATE", "Trimmed ATE", "ATT", "ATO"))
  mx <- aggregate(w ~ estimand, wd, max)
  ggplot(wd, aes(estimand, w)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "#0072B2", colour = NA, alpha = 0.5, scale = "width") +
    geom_point(data = mx, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = mx, aes(label = sprintf("max %.1f", w)),
              vjust = -0.8, colour = "#D55E00", size = 5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
    scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.001, 900)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "implied weight (log scale)") + thm
}
```

## The estimand ladder

- Changing the estimand after seeing results is not acceptable. Refusing to change it ever means throwing away studies that could answer a slightly different question.
- So the rule is written down first: the primary estimand, the fallbacks in order, and the overlap verdict that triggers a move down the list.
- If the primary is not feasible, the software will not estimate it unless someone gives a reason, and the reason is logged.

## The support map: simulating without the outcome

Resample the covariates, draw treatment from the fitted propensity model, and simulate outcomes from a prespecified set of outcome models. The true effect is known in every simulated dataset, so each estimand's estimator can be scored.

![C1: the ATE fails at the mildest surface](../rescueCo/results/multiarm/fig_supportmap_C1.png)

## Why treatment is redrawn rather than kept

- Most plasmode simulations keep each person's observed treatment and only simulate the outcome.
- Shaw et al. (2025) showed that this builds a positivity violation into the simulation: a group that was all treated in the real data stays all treated in every simulated dataset.
- That is a problem here, because the positivity violation is the thing we want to measure. So cleanTMLE draws treatment from the fitted propensity model instead. The case study compares both approaches.

## The same simulation loop tests the estimator

The candidate estimators are re-run under data problems that were declared in advance: missing covariates, misclassified exposure or outcome, poor overlap, and an unmeasured confounder. The selection rule picks the candidate whose worst case is least bad.

![Degradation gradient, earlier single-contrast lock](../rescueCo/results/manuscript_artifacts/fig_dq_gradient.png)

## What the software can and cannot do

Can: keep the outcome out of the design stage, log every decision inside a hashed lock, and flag estimates that contradict the raw data.

Cannot: stop someone with raw-data access from looking at the outcome elsewhere, check how variables were measured, or detect a confounder that was never recorded. Those need institutional controls.

# 3. What the simulations showed

## Three scenarios, six estimators

- 2,000 people per dataset, 200 datasets per scenario.
- Scenario A: good overlap. B: marginal overlap. C: an unmeasured confounder.
- Estimators: crude, matching, IPTW, TMLE, cross-validated TMLE, matched TMLE.

With good overlap every adjusted estimator recovers the truth. With marginal overlap, bias stays small, but the IPTW and matched-TMLE intervals are too wide because their variance formulas treat the propensity score as known. A bootstrap fixes that, and the workflow flags it before unblinding.

## Same estimators, different workflow

In scenario C every estimator is biased in the same direction, TMLE least so. The software did not find the hidden confounder. It stopped because one of the prespecified stress scenarios failed its threshold.

| Scenario | Traditional analyst | Outcome-blind workflow |
|---|---|---|
| Good overlap | Diagnostics look fine; report the result. | Same, and the simulation confirms the candidates. Proceed. |
| Marginal overlap | A careful analyst notices and adapts. Many do not. | The variance problem is measured before unblinding. Proceed with a caveat. |
| Unmeasured confounding | All adjusted estimates agree with each other; a wrong null result gets published. | The confounding stress scenario fails the bias threshold. Stop. |

# 4. Case study: Rescue.Co, Nairobi

## Five contrasts, one registry

8,323 trauma patients with a known mode of transport, three Nairobi hospitals, 2018 to 2024. Each contrast gets its own lock on the same cohort, with the same 90 design variables and the same estimand ladder. Outcomes: death within six months, and time to arrival at hospital.

| Lock | Comparison | N | Treated |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| C1 | Rescue.Co vs everyone else (protocol comparator) | 8,323 | 1,039 |
| C2 | Rescue.Co vs non-ambulance | 7,165 | 1,039 |
| C3 | Any ambulance vs non-ambulance | 8,323 | 2,197 |
| C4 | Rescue.Co vs other ambulance, transfers included | 2,197 | 1,039 |
| Primary | Rescue.Co vs other ambulance, transfers and prior care excluded | 1,616 | 1,003 |

## What poor overlap looks like

:::

## The support verdicts

On the protocol contrast, two-fifths of the sample falls outside the acceptable propensity band. C1 and C2 both trip the SEVERE trigger, before any outcome data are attached.

```{r fig-support, fig.cap = "Share of each contrast outside the propensity band [0.05, 0.95]. Dotted lines mark the verdict thresholds: FLAG above 1%, SEVERE above 25%. Labels give the largest implied ATE weight."}
if (!is.null(cs_sup)) {
  sp <- cs_sup
  sp$contrast[sp$contrast == "PRIMARY"] <- "Primary"
  sp$contrast <- factor(sp$contrast,
                        levels = rev(c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "Primary")))
  sp$verdict <- factor(sp$verdict, levels = names(okabe))
  ggplot(sp, aes(pct_outside_band, contrast, colour = verdict)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(1, 25), linetype = "dotted",
               colour = "grey55") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = pct_outside_band), linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_point(size = 5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("max weight %.0f", max_iptw_weight)),
              hjust = -0.15, vjust = -0.9, size = 5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = okabe, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 62)) +
    labs(x = "% of sample outside propensity band [0.05, 0.95]", y = NULL) +
    thm
}
```

## Who never gets a Rescue.Co ambulance?

The tree search identifies the groups behind the C1 overlap problem:

- injured at a private home: 1,386 patients, 1.4% treated
- other non-street injury locations: 1,438 patients, 2.5% treated
- assault victims elsewhere: 1,062 patients, 4.2% treated

The data say almost nothing about what would happen if these patients had used Rescue.Co. Trimming to the overlap region removes 3,377 people, nearly all controls. Compared with the patients kept, they are more often injured at home (40% versus 1%), more often assaulted, younger, and further from hospital.

## Which estimands survive the C1 fit

The data can support an estimate. It is an estimate of a different quantity from the one the protocol named.

| Estimand | Max weight | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| ATE | 257 | SEVERE, infeasible |
| Trimmed ATE | 20 | PASS, population changes |
| ATT | 5.0 | PASS |
| ATO | 1.0 | PASS |
| Matched ATT | 1.0 | PASS, 95% of treated matched |

## The cohort exclusions removed the confounding

Both negative controls show an association in the full cohort and none after the prespecified exclusion of transferred patients. On C1 the urban-household control shows an association at every level of restriction. Two controls were too rare to estimate and are reported as such.

```{r fig-nc, fig.cap = "Two socioeconomic negative controls on the transfers-included contrast, refit on each nested cohort. Points are unadjusted risk differences with 95% intervals."}
if (!is.null(cs_ncl)) {
  nc <- cs_ncl[cs_ncl$contrast == "C4" &
               cs_ncl$negative_control %in%
                 c("nc_household_urban", "nc_cooking_fuel_wood_charcoal") &
               cs_ncl$status == "estimated", ]
  nc$control <- ifelse(grepl("urban", nc$negative_control),
                       "urban household", "wood or charcoal fuel")
  nc$rung <- factor(nc$cohort,
                    levels = c("full cohort", "transfers excluded",
                               "transfers and prior care excluded"),
                    labels = c("full cohort\n(n = 2,197)",
                               "transfers excluded\n(n = 1,703)",
                               "+ prior care excluded\n(n = 1,616)"))
  pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.35)
  ggplot(nc, aes(rung, estimate, colour = control, group = control)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55") +
    geom_line(position = pd, linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.12,
                  position = pd, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 4, position = pd) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#CC79A7"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "risk difference") + thm
}
```

## Care-process variables are left out of the adjustment set

Whether vital signs were recorded within an hour, and whether blood pressure is missing, both depend on treatment in three of the five contrasts (standardised differences up to 0.34). The mode of transport changes what happens at the hospital.

Adjusting for them would introduce collider bias through in-hospital care, so they are excluded, and the check records the reason.

## The pre-outcome decisions

All of these decisions were made before the outcome data were attached.

| Contrast | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Primary | Proceed |
| C3, C4 | Proceed, FLAG caveat attached |
| C1, C2 | Proceed with a caveat. The ATE is not supported; the ladder moves to the trimmed ATE, then ATT, then ATO, and the SEVERE verdict is logged as the reason |

## Six-month mortality, down the ladder

C2 reports no ATE at all. The C1 ATE appears once, as a logged override kept so the two pipelines can be compared. It carries its SEVERE label and a standard error several times larger than the other rows.

```{r fig-forest, fig.cap = "Risk differences with 95% intervals, one row per feasible estimand per contrast. Negative favours Rescue.Co."}
if (!is.null(cs_lad) && any(grepl("death", cs_lad$outcome))) {
  ld <- cs_lad[grepl("death", cs_lad$outcome), ]
  ld$contrast[ld$contrast == "PRIMARY"] <- "Primary"
  ld$estimand <- sub("^trimmed_ATE$", "Trimmed ATE", ld$estimand)
  ld$row <- paste(ld$contrast, ld$estimand)
  ld$row <- factor(ld$row, levels = rev(unique(ld$row)))
  ggplot(ld, aes(estimate, row, colour = contrast)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), width = 0.18,
                  linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#E69F00",
                                   "#CC79A7", "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "risk difference, six-month mortality", y = NULL) + thm
} else {
  plot.new(); text(0.5, 0.5, "Estimation chain running; fills on render.")
}
```

```{r effects-note, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(cs_lad)) {
  n_pairs <- length(unique(paste(cs_lad$contrast, cs_lad$outcome)))
  if (n_pairs < 10)
    cat("*", n_pairs, "of 10 contrast-outcome pairs completed so far;",
        "the figure fills as the chain lands.*")
}
```

## Time to arrival, re-analysed

This is the outcome that once gave +14,637 minutes. The estimands with bounded weights now agree that Rescue.Co arrives three to four and a half hours sooner. Every row is checked against the raw group means, and that check alone would have caught the original result.

```{r tta-table, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(cs_lad) && any(grepl("time_to_arrival", cs_lad$outcome))) {
  ld <- cs_lad[grepl("time_to_arrival", cs_lad$outcome),
               intersect(c("contrast", "estimand", "estimate",
                           "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "implausible"),
                         names(cs_lad))]
  for (cn in c("estimate", "ci_lower", "ci_upper"))
    ld[[cn]] <- sprintf("%.1f", as.numeric(ld[[cn]]))
  names(ld) <- c("Contrast", "Estimand", "Minutes", "CI lower",
                 "CI upper", "Flagged")[seq_along(names(ld))]
  cat(knitr::kable(ld, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE), sep = "\n")
} else {
  cat("*Estimation in progress. This slide fills with the",
      "time-to-arrival ladder rows.*")
}
```

## Keeping the observed treatment, on real data

A support map that kept the observed treatment would have declared the sound designs infeasible too.

```{r fig-designcmp, fig.cap = "Coverage under the stressed outcome surface, 200 replicates per design. Keeping the observed treatment degrades every estimand, on the sound design too."}
if (!is.null(cs_cmp)) {
  dc <- cs_cmp[cs_cmp$confounding == 2 & cs_cmp$modification == 0, ]
  dc$design <- ifelse(dc$design == "generate_treatment",
                      "treatment redrawn", "observed treatment kept")
  dc$estimand <- sub("^trimmed_ATE$", "Trimmed ATE",
                     sub("^matched_ATT$", "Matched ATT", dc$estimand))
  dc$estimand <- factor(dc$estimand, levels = rev(c(
    "ATE", "Trimmed ATE", "ATT", "ATO", "Matched ATT")))
  ggplot(dc, aes(coverage, estimand, colour = design)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.90, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey55") +
    geom_line(aes(group = estimand), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 4.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ contrast) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`treatment redrawn` = "#0072B2",
                                   `observed treatment kept` = "#D55E00"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.55, 1)) +
    labs(x = "95% interval coverage under stress", y = NULL) + thm
}
```

## The record showed an earlier mistake of ours

- The first single-contrast run used a primary outcome with 92% prevalence, the common category of a two-level variable.
- The cohort-adequacy check recorded a stop. The pipeline went ahead anyway, and nothing recorded why.
- The rebuild found this because both entries were still in the record, a stop followed by an estimate with nothing in between.
- Mortality is now the primary outcome, and an override cannot be recorded without a reason.

## What a reviewer can check

- Every verdict, declaration, and estimand switch was logged before the outcome data were attached.
- The protocol's primary comparison was refused, and the reason is in the record. Each reported estimate says which population it applies to.
- Where the two pipelines overlap, the clean-room estimates agree with the parallel unblinded analysis to within a fraction of a standard error. The comparison is published row by row.

# 5. Compared with existing tools

## Side by side

TMLE has been around for over a decade and the staged design is published guidance. What is new here is checking whether the comparison can be estimated during the blind phase, and keeping a record of when that was checked.

| Feature | TMLE packages | causalRisk | Clean-room papers | cleanTMLE |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Targeted-learning estimation | yes | -- | -- | yes |
| Cohort grammar, cumulative-risk reporting | partial | yes | -- | yes |
| Graded support verdict, per-estimand feasibility | -- | -- | -- | yes |
| Pre-registered estimand ladder, logged switching | -- | -- | -- | yes |
| Outcome-blind support map | -- | -- | -- | yes |
| Plasmode candidate selection, DQ stress test | -- | -- | -- | yes |
| Fingerprinted lock and design log | -- | -- | guidance | yes |

## When to use it, and what it does not do

Use it when someone will ask whether an analytic decision was made before or after you saw the result.

It does not design the study, check the data or the outcome definitions, or replace negative controls and post-outcome sensitivity analyses. For confirmatory work it should sit inside institutional governance, with separate roles and independent review. If an institution wants the sign-off enforced in software, `enforce = TRUE` blocks estimation until a named person unmasks the outcome.

## Where I want input

1. The harshest support-map scenarios look the same as strong unmeasured confounding, so a rule that requires passing the whole grid mixes up two different problems. How should the plausible range be chosen and written down in advance?
2. Is SEVERE the right default trigger, and is trimmed ATE, then ATT, then ATO the right order?
3. How should the stress-test severity ranges be documented so that a reviewer accepts them?
4. The matched ATT is the most stable estimand in every map and the hardest population to describe. Should it be a sensitivity analysis or a candidate primary?

## Resources

- Package: <https://github.com/amertens/cleanTMLE> (v0.3.0)
- Manuscript draft: `reports/manuscript_outcome_blind_dq.qmd`
- Case-study artifacts: `rescueCo/results/multiarm/`
- Vignettes: get started (five verbs), and the full workflow
- Tutorial: `tutorials/clean_room_targeted_learning_tutorial.qmd`

Questions welcome.

# Appendix A: Concepts and alignment

## Conceptual layers in the staged workflow

| Layer | Description |
|---|---|
| Causal question | Clinical or policy question framed as a target trial. |
| Causal estimand | Counterfactual effect of interest, e.g. marginal risk difference. |
| Identification assumptions | Conditions under which the estimand equals an observed-data parameter. |
| Statistical estimand | That observed-data parameter. |
| Estimand ladder | Pre-registered fallbacks and the verdict that triggers a switch. |
| Estimator | TMLE, IPTW, matching. |
| Pre-outcome diagnostic | Support verdict, feasibility, simulated bias and coverage, balance, negative controls. |
| Governance decision | Proceed, proceed with qualification, or stop (Muntner et al. 2024). |

## The causal roadmap, and what the package covers

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["1. Causal question and target trial"] --> B["2. Observed data and source characterisation"]
    B --> C["3. Identification assumptions"]
    C --> D["4. Statistical estimand + declared ladder"]
    D --> E["5. Lock candidate estimators and thresholds"]
    E --> F["Design stage: support, feasibility, support map, plasmode, DQ stress, negative controls"]
    F --> G["Design report: proceed / qualify / stop"]
    G --> H["Estimate the declared primary and feasible fallbacks"]
    H --> I["Post-outcome sensitivity: E-value, delta, QBA"]
    I --> J["Interpretation and transportability"]
    style C fill:#e6e6e6,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style D fill:#e6e6e6,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style E fill:#e6e6e6,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style F fill:#e6e6e6,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style G fill:#e6e6e6,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style H fill:#e6e6e6,stroke:#333,color:#000
```

## Regulatory alignment (excerpt)

| Roadmap component | FDA / EMA / ICH anchor | cleanTMLE |
|---|---|---|
| Causal question | Target-trial framework; FDA RWE Framework; ICH M14 | Lock record; `design_report(protocol = ...)` emulation table |
| Identification (positivity) | ICH E9(R1) | `assess_support()`, `estimand_feasibility()` |
| Statistical estimand | ICH E9(R1); FDA RWE Considerations | `declare_estimand_ladder()`, `run_estimand_ladder()` |
| Estimator selection | FDA non-interventional studies; ICH M14 | `define_candidates()`, `select_candidate()` |
| Pre-outcome DQ stress | Source reliability (FDA, EMA) | `stress_test()`, `simulate_support()` |
| Post-outcome sensitivity | FDA non-interventional; ICH E9(R1) | `compute_evalue()`, `run_delta_sensitivity()` |

## The stress-test threat families

| Threat | Mechanism | Probes | Does not probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Covariate missingness | MCAR, MAR, MNAR masks; median impute | Imputation robustness | Phenotype validity |
| Exposure misclassification | Flip A at given sens and spec | Treatment measurement | Differential error by outcome |
| Outcome misclassification | Flip Y, optionally per arm | Outcome measurement | Time-varying ascertainment |
| Near-positivity | Amplify covariate-treatment association | Estimator strain | The realised design's support |
| Unmeasured confounding | Latent U shifts A and Y | Exchangeability | Multiple latent confounders |

# Appendix B: Case-study detail

## The declared ladder, per lock

The same for all five locks, declared before outcome access: primary ATE with IPCW for missing outcomes; fallbacks trimmed ATE [0.05, 0.95], then ATT, then ATO; trigger SEVERE. The matched ATT appears in the feasibility table and support map as a design-stage sensitivity analysis and is not estimated on the ladder.

Propensity library: the `build_sl_library()` preset for wide registry designs (penalised logistic learners, PCA-reduced GLMs, marginal mean; no tree learners, which can separate arms on wide indicator sets), ten folds.

## Negative-control ladder, exact rows

Hypertension is null on every rung. Insulin-treated diabetes and HIV on ART are inestimable (a cell below 5 events) and labelled as such. A TMLE-adjusted variant is released with a caveat: on restricted rungs it conditions on design columns that are near-copies of the socioeconomic controls.

| Contrast | Cohort | Urban household | Wood or charcoal fuel |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| C4 | Full (n = 2,197) | +0.068 | -0.052 |
| C4 | Transfers excluded (n = 1,703) | +0.001 | +0.000 |
| C4 | Prior care also excluded (n = 1,616) | -0.003 | -0.001 |
| C1 | Full (n = 8,323) | +0.013 | -0.006 |

## The support-map reading rule, from the design log

Recorded before estimation: the maps are read over the moderate-confounding region (simulated confounding strength up to 1), with the whole-grid pass reported as a conservative bound.

The harshest rung stresses every weighting-based estimand at once, including on the PASS-verdict primary cohort, so a whole-grid rule conflates support failure with confounding stress. The signature used instead: failure at the mildest surface means a support problem (C1's ATE, coverage 0.87 before any simulated confounding); failure only under stress, hitting all unmatched estimands together, means stress (the primary cohort at strength 2, where the matched ATT holds 0.93 to 0.96).

## Candidate selection under stress (earlier single-contrast lock)

Four TMLE candidates varying propensity library and truncation tie on the clean baseline (RMSE within 0.0002), where the minimum-RMSE rule would lock `glm_t01`. Under the five-threat sweep the worst-case RMSE ratios separate: 1.82, 1.73, 1.53, and 1.27 for `ensemble_t05`.

The minimax rule locks `ensemble_t05`. The candidate that looked best on clean data did worst under the prespecified stress scenarios. This was run with 50 replicates to illustrate the workflow; 200 is the bar for drawing conclusions.

## Effect estimates, exact rows

```{r effects-table-appendix, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(cs_lad) && any(grepl("death", cs_lad$outcome))) {
  ld <- cs_lad[grepl("death", cs_lad$outcome),
               intersect(c("contrast", "estimand", "n", "estimate",
                           "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "p_value",
                           "support_verdict"), names(cs_lad))]
  for (cn in c("estimate", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "p_value"))
    ld[[cn]] <- sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(ld[[cn]]))
  names(ld) <- c("Contrast", "Estimand", "N", "RD", "CI lower", "CI upper",
                 "p", "Support")[seq_along(names(ld))]
  cat(knitr::kable(ld, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE), sep = "\n")
} else {
  cat("*Fills from the estimation outputs on render.*")
}
```
